filename: PYROCAST_ a Machine Learning Pipeline to Forecast Pyrocumulonimbus (PyroCb) Clouds.pdf
title: PYROCAST: a Machine Learning Pipeline to Forecast Pyrocumulonimbus (PyroCb) Clouds
venue: Tackling Climate Change with Machine Learning: workshop at NeurIPS 2022
code_availability: Code and data are available at https://doi.org/10.56272/fpib2524
testbed_rationale: The dataset is designed for event detection and short-term (6-hour) wildfire pyroconvection forecasting rather than atmospheric parameterization or climate model emulation.
pain_points: Limited sample size of extreme pyroCb events (~84 events / ~6k observations used in training), leading to rapid overfitting in deep CNN models
Heavy class imbalance requiring weighting in tree splitting
Lower predictive skill when pyroconvection is already active compared to when no convection is yet visible
Practical limitation of the 'weather oracle' setup when replaced by real weather forecasts
extraction_notes: The paper is a workshop contribution at NeurIPS 2022 (Climate Change AI workshop) describing a detection and forecasting pipeline. A companion workshop paper focuses on the causal discovery framework.
